newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's top drug lord probably dead - government.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's top drug lord probably dead - government.

text.p: Mexico's most wanted drug lord, who eluded countless police raids and an eight-year manhunt, appeared on Sunday to have a died from botched plastic surgery.

Mexican authorities referred in a statement on Saturday night to the "probable death of the drug trafficker Amado Carrillo Fuentes." But they said they needed more tests to confirm the identity of a man who died of a heart attack after plastic surgery and liposuction on Friday night in a private Mexico City clinic.

Callers to Mexican radio stations said they suspected some sort of trick but the family of the drug lord, nicknamed "Lord of the Skies" for his ability to fly cocaine-laden jets from Colombia to northern Mexico, were in no doubt about his death.

Nor were the hordes of smartly dressed men, some in snakeskin boots and cowboy hats, who arrived in brand-new four-wheel-drive vehicles with darkened windows at the luxury family ranch. They had gone to the village of Guamuchilito in northwestern Mexico to deliver 8-foot (2.2-metre)-high floral wreaths and offer condolences.
Aurora Fuentes de Carrillo arrived sobbing with her three daughters at the San Martin funeral parlour in the state capital, Culiacan, on Saturday night to identify a body in a gray metal coffin.
"Yes, it's my son," she cried to waiting reporters.

Moments later scores of heavily armed police, some in plainclothes, others toting submachine guns, descended on the funeral parlour. After a furious argument with the family, they removed the body under heavy security and shipped it from Sinaloa's main airport at Culiacan, apparently to Mexico City.
"I hope to God this never happens to you. They don't know how to respect the grief of others," Fuentes screamed.
The Attorney General's Office refused on Sunday to say where the body was or announce any results of tests on it.

Mexico is traditionally extremely secretive about drug issues. Authorities appeared anxious not to allow the apparent bizarre accidental death of their most wanted fugitive right under their noses in the capital to overshadow national elections being held on Sunday.

In the only offical information so far, the Attorney General's Office said in a statement on Saturday night that a man had been admitted to the Santa Monica hospital, a small, exclusive clinic in Mexico City's smart Polanco district, on Thursday under the name of Antonio Flores Montes for extensive facial plastic surgery and liposuction.
After an eight-hour operation on Friday, the patient was taken to Room 407 of the hospital, where a duty doctor found him dead in bed at 6 p.m., the statement said.
A certificate in the name of Antonio Flores, aged 42, gave the cause of death as a heart attack. The body was flown on Saturday morning to Culiacan and sent to the funeral parlour.

The Attorney General's Office said it had carried out an autopsy and fingerprint tests. "Although from the tests carried out so far there are indications that the body which allegedly belongs to Antonio Flores Montes is really that of Amado Carrillo Fuentes, the (office) cannot, at the moment, affirm this with total certainty," it said.

Carrillo, believed to be 42 years old, was born into a poor peasant family but rose fast to become a drug superstar. As Mexican cartels evolved from being middlemen for Colombian cocaine shipments to big traffickers in their own right, his cartel, centred on the Mexican border town of Ciudad Juarez, gained in might.

Thomas Constantine, the head of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, described Carrillo in June 1996 as "the most powerful figure in the Mexican drug trade." Carrillo was the subject of at least 26 separate DEA investigations.

Mexico's former anti-drug chief, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, was jailed in February on charges he had taken bribes from Carrillo, including a luxury apartment for his mistress, armoured cars, scrambler phones and money.

The last confirmed sighting of the capo was in January, when a videotape showed him attending the wedding of his sister at the Guamuchilito ranch. Police and troops raided the reception after the ceremony but Carrillo escaped, apparently after being tipped off about the raid.
